newsitem.title: UK: Latin America and Asia driving music sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Latin America and Asia driving music sales growth.

text.p: Emerging markets in Latin America and Asia are fuelling growth in the $40 billion global music business, according to a report released on Wednesday.
Developing markets accounted for 70 percent of growth in 1996, against only 20 percent in 1993, trade body the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI) said in its study.

Latin America and Asia are the most important developing markets although the two regions still contributed only six percent each of total world sales in 1996. Unit sales rose 20 percent in Latin America last year, the fastest growth rate anywhere in the world.

Annual global sales growth has averaged five percent over the past five years. But real growth in value, excluding the effects of inflation, fell to just two percent in 1996 from a peak of 11 percent in 1994.
The global music industry is dominated by five major international players -- PolyGram NV, EMI Group Plc, Sony, Bertelsmann and Warner Bros.
The slowdown in growth has prompted a painful round of restructuring, with the majors shedding jobs and cutting costs as they attempt to adapt to life after the gold rush.

Unit sales in the U.S. market shrank by seven percent last year, the report said. But the U.S. still heads the global charts, annual sales topping $12 billion in 1996, almost double those of Japan, the world's second largest market followed by Germany, Britain, France and Brazil.

The compact disc (CD) has continued its unstoppable rise, sales more than doubling over the five-year period to 2.1 billion units in 1996. The demise of vinyl appears to be almost complete, sales of old-format LPs dwindling to just 21 million last year.
Britons emerge as the world's biggest music fans, buying an average of four albums each per year.

At the other end of the scale, Africa is identified as a massively underdeveloped market. The continent had sales last year of $250 million -- roughly the equivalent of those of a small European country such as Norway.
